name: SQLite SQL dialect
title: SQLite SQL dialect (3.54)

type.text: **The value decides the type, not the column**: type affinity coerces on write and comparison, one column stores numbers, text, and blobs side by side, and a mismatch is a data fact found at run time
**No sum types**: an alternative is a nullable column or a conventionally tagged value, and the consumer re-derives the encoding
**No generic parameter**: queries are typed per statement, and a parameterized "any table" query does not exist in the language
**NULL is a member of every domain**: any column accepts NULL unless declared, three-valued logic decides comparisons, and no signature records the guard
**Statements state no effect**: an INSERT, an UPDATE, and a SELECT look alike to the caller, and nothing tracks what a statement touches
**The extension boundary is unchecked**: load_extension() loads a compiled shared object in process, and the agreement on entry points and ABI is checked by neither side's compiler

construction.text: **Any value fits any column by default**: ordinary tables coerce or store whatever arrives, and STRICT tables — the construct that enforces declared types — are an opt-in the deployment must choose

memory.text: **Allocation is the library's**: pages, cache, and statement memory live inside the embedding process under the engine's allocator, and the SQL text allocates nothing

error.text: **Errors are integer codes out of the call**: the language raises none and catches none — the result codes return to the host, and the SQL text carries no branch for them

concurrency.text: **Concurrency is the engine's**: WAL mode, locking modes, and busy handlers decide what runs in parallel, and the SQL text names none of it

platform.text: **The query runs only in SQLite-family engines**: the dialect, the pragmas, and the file format are one engine's, and nothing in the language runs without an embedding
**A poor fit outside application storage**: the language has no stored procedures, no users, and no network story, and application logic beyond local persistence builds every abstraction itself

performance.text: **The plan is a statement away**: EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN are part of the published reference, so a query can be asked to show its plan before it runs

ecosystem.text: **No package manager exists for extensions**: load_extension() takes a path, distribution is find-the-URL-and-trust-it, and no registry, namespace, or signing channel stands behind the ecosystem

evolution.text: **Conservatism is the stated policy**: release notes document deliberate stability across decades, and the same policy promises forward the quirks — affinity and quoting — a new project might rather not inherit

domain.text: **Adopting SQLite SQL means adopting the file format**: pragmas, affinity, and the single-file model define what a query can say, and the same vocabulary is the application's storage design

learning.text: **The reference assumes the C embedder**: the docs' structure follows the library's interfaces rather than a language course, and affinity and quoting rules live where a C programmer would look for them

syntax.text: **The same text means two things**: double-quoted strings may be identifiers or literals depending on schema state and the DQS setting, and affinity decides whether '5' equals 5 — inconsistencies the docs document as compatibility behavior

testing.text: **No standard test harness for user SQL**: the project's own TH3 and sqllogic tests are internal, and the documented testing story is application-side tests against the library
**The plan is queryable in the CLI**: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN runs in the ordinary shell, published as part of the language reference

security.text: **Dynamic typing is the security margin**: affinity coercion meets attacker-shaped values at evaluation, and type confusions across the C boundary are the documented risk class
**String-built SQL is the canonical injection**: the docs' own guidance exists because SQL text assembled by concatenation reaches the parser; the mitigation is bound parameters
**Overflow promotes in silence**: integer arithmetic that would overflow "perform[s] floating point arithmetic, per IEEE Standard 754", so the value changes above 2^53 with no failure

reproducibility.text: **A query is text against a file**: the same SQL on the same file and library version reproduces the same answer, and nothing is built
**No toolchain pin exists in the official distribution**: the repository names no library version, and the embedding's amalgamation or system copy decides semantics

supplychain.text: **No signed provenance for published extensions or builds**: the download page publishes hashes of official artifacts, but extensions and third-party bindings carry no signature-checked distribution channel
**No advisory feed names the ecosystem's dependencies**: fixes land in release notes and the security page, with no CVE-mapped advisory database for extensions and bindings

observability.text: **No tracing standard is part of the language**: the profile and trace callbacks are C API features, and the SQL text carries no trace hook
**No structured logging in the language**: the error log is a C callback, and no logging construct exists in the SQL surface

feedback.text: **No debugger exists for SQL**: diagnosis goes through EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN, the CLI's dot commands, and result codes returned to the host

interop.text: **No portable target**: the query runs on a SQLite-family engine, and nothing in the language runs without an embedding

governance.text: **Governance is one project lead and a small consortium**: the direction, the releases, and the format promises are the SQLite project's, and no independent body can change them
**No public specification exists**: the language reference documents the implemented behavior of one engine, and no independent implementation follows from a published standard
**Correctness is what the library does**: no conformance suite exists for the dialect, and the one implementation is the oracle

tradeoffs: **One file is the whole database**: the format is stable, cross-platform, and promised backward compatible for all future 3.x releases, and the price is a format whose forward direction is only "usually" compatible and whose rules live in one implementation
**Flexibility by default, strictness by opt-in**: any column accepts any value until STRICT is chosen, and the price is a schema that describes rather than enforces
**The C boundary is the feature and the exposure**: load_extension() and the amalgamation make embedding trivial, and the price is an unchecked ABI agreement and a supply line with no registry
**Stability is the roadmap**: decades of release notes document deliberate conservatism, and the price is that the dialect's quirks — affinity, DQS quoting — are promised forward as behavior
verdict: SQLite's SQL dialect is the language of an embedded, public-domain library: standard-shaped SQL with type affinity instead of enforced types, opt-in STRICT tables, pragmas as the control plane, load_extension() as the only in-process escape, and one database file as the whole deployment. Its costs are the embedded model's own: values decide types at run time, NULL in every domain, silent float promotion on integer overflow, a canonical string-built injection surface, and an extension ecosystem with no registry, namespace, or signing. Main strengths: EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN in the ordinary shell, a file format whose backward compatibility is an explicit published promise, decades-long stability as a stated policy, and public-domain source. Main weaknesses: no stored procedures, no debugger, no standard test harness, no structured logging or tracing in the language, single-project governance with no specification or conformance suite, and inconsistency the docs themselves carry as compatibility behavior.

energy.text: Energy is the embedding process's: the library's cache and locks share the application's fate, and the reader's levers are schema and index design the SQL text exposes but does not control.

ai-readiness.text: SQLite is a common agent-side store and SQL is the model-trained lingua franca — generated queries meet the traps: affinity coercion, three-valued logic, and pragma state the text never names.

safety.text: No certified path; durability and atomicity are the engine's guarantees, stated in its own documentation, with the project's release discipline as the only contract.

use:query.observation: EXPLAIN and EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN are part of the published reference

use:embedded.observation: nothing in the language runs without an embedding

platform:embedded.observation: the library's cache and locks share the application's fate

delivery.note: queries travel as text to the library, which parses and executes them in place; views and triggers are stored as source; no compiled unit is produced
extensions are compiled shared objects a consumer loads without rebuilding; no published document states a cross-release linking rule, so the boundary is recorded and prices nothing
the official distribution ships C source the consumer compiles inside its own build

data_formats.note: the file-format page publishes the promise ("all releases of SQLite version 3 can read and write database files created by the very first SQLite 3 release... The developers promise to maintain backwards compatibility") and states the limit of the forward direction ("SQLite is usually, but not completely forwards compatible")
